alignments.note: Predicate adjective in a comparative clause; the construction-supplied copula joins the predicate under rule 20, headed on 'better'.

ASV italic 'good' before 'name'; the clause's two ṭôḇ morphemes are already spent on 'is better' and on 'precious', so no morpheme licenses this word (rule 30). Competing reading: treat 'good ... is better' as one discontinuous realization of s001 under rule 25; the italic corroborates the added reading without deciding it (rule 7).
Supplied indefinite article joins the noun it determines (rule 15).
Attributive ṭôḇ on the ointment, rendered 'precious'.
Waw takes the 'and' written for it (rule 14).
Article on the rectum takes the phrase's single written 'the', which English fronts to the left edge of an anarthrously rendered chain (rule 29).
Construct noun keeps only its own word; its 'the' is the rectum's article, fronted.
Relational 'of' belongs to the nomen rectum (rule 19).
No article morpheme here, so the construct takes a supplied 'the' (rule 29).
Infinitive construct is the rectum and takes the relational 'of' with its own lexeme 'birth' (rule 19).
Suffix realized by the generalizing possessive "one's" (rule 18).

review_notes: Both min units take a bare 'than'; the comparative force of ṭôḇ is carried by 'is better' on the adjective.
The one contested unit is the italicized 'good' (t002), marked added; the alternative is a twice-realized s001.
